full_description: Queue claim atomicity — claim+move-to-remediating is one atomic op.
Size-stratified fairness + tier ordering (routing is deterministic).
Preemption-requeue priority preservation (the ONLY sanctioned requeue).

short_description: Cancellation removes from ALL 9 Redis structures + chunk purge.
full_description: Cancellation removes from ALL 9 Redis structures + chunk purge.
Metric/queue-depth consistency under queue-shape change (structural).
Wake/sleep ↔ in-flight (split-brain + version gating) — one guard.
Stale-sweep ↔ heartbeat — don't kill a still-progressing job.
Progress monotonicity under concurrent writers (Lua-atomic guard).
Chunk fan-out/fan-in aggregate — dual-completer merge-claim CAS.
Cross-SOA partial-failure mid-sequence — typed FailureCause branch.
Upload-before-DB-update on corrupt-output fallback (SM ordering).
No-DROP under the bridge — ack on handler-return AFTER the terminal write (the message lease spans the whole process).
No-DOUBLE (credit) — the quota-gate at-most-once billing fence: a redelivered check never double-reserves credits.
No-DOUBLE (chunk fan-out) — the introducer at-most-once parent-claim CAS: a redelivered introduce never double-fans-out.

short_description: Producer publishes STRAIGHT to the managed queue
full_description: Producer publishes STRAIGHT to the managed queue — no Redis-in-the-path bridge (single ordered publish per event).
Orphan-recovery relocation preserves no-double-merge — the lost-notify safety net (boot-scan → Cloud Scheduler cron) still gates the merge on the completer SQL-CAS.

Async-cutover eventual termination — under min=0 + at-least-once PUSH (delivery may be LOST) with the always-on polling supervisor GONE, every SUBMITTED job EVENTUALLY reaches a terminal state; the Cloud Scheduler sweep-cron is the load-bearing recovery driver.

GCP-timer-INDEPENDENT scale-to-zero resume — a scaled-to-zero (minScale=0) consumer's enqueued job ALWAYS reaches a terminal (done) state and is processed AT MOST ONCE, across every interleaving of {observable wake, durable-claim CAS, redeliver, drop, async-loss, owned-cron sweep}; completion holds even when EVERY cold-wake delivery loses its post-ACK async work — the owned Cloud-Scheduler sweep-net carries it, so resume NEVER depends on winning a race against a GCP-opaque timer/deadline.

short_description: Fan-out re-drive completeness — a WAITING parent NEVER has a permanently-absent chunk task: [](WAITING ⇒ ∀c: dispatched_durably(c) ∨ redrive_pending(c)).
full_description: Fan-out re-drive completeness — a WAITING parent NEVER has a permanently-absent chunk task: [](WAITING ⇒ ∀c: dispatched_durably(c) ∨ redrive_pending(c)). The missing-set (the durably-absent chunk TASKS, keyed on the chunk-ROW (status, started_at) — NOT a Cloud-Tasks task-existence query, which does not exist, G1) is always re-driven via a BLIND idempotent re-create (name-dedup convergent); on re-drive-budget exhaustion past the FANOUT_STALL_SECONDS window the fan-out watchdog sweep FAILs the parent (WAITING→FAILED, M4). FIDELITY GUARD (Q3): the re-drive targets ONLY missing TASKS keyed on the chunk-ROW state — a COMPLETED or leased/REMEDIATING chunk is NEVER re-created (never re-remediates a delivered chunk; a leased chunk counts as dispatched → no false-timeout).

short_description: Fan-out eventual termination (INV-18 fan-out extension, G3)
full_description: Fan-out eventual termination (INV-18 fan-out extension, G3) — every chunk of a WAITING parent EVENTUALLY reaches a terminal state: WaitingWithMissingChunks ~> AllChunksTerminal. This is the fan-OUT liveness INV-18 does NOT express: INV-18 (Submitted ~> Terminal) DELIBERATELY FOLDS chunk cardinality into one job-level token to keep its TLC state space tractable (G3: do NOT un-fold it). A NEW invariant with its OWN small .tla keeps INV-18 = job-level and INV-FO-2 = fan-out-level, each spec small. Under min=0 + at-least-once managed publish, a chunk task may be LOST (partial publish / created-but-undelivered); the fan-out watchdog sweep (the ONE always-reachable driver) re-finds the stranded parent and re-drives its missing chunks — WITHOUT the sweep a lost chunk task strands the parent in WAITING forever (the falsifiability teeth).

Frontier-state derivability — a job's FrontierState (UNPLANNED/PLANNED/EXHAUSTED/FINALIZED) is a PURE, TOTAL, deterministic function of its durable rows (jobs.planned_at + jobs.status + the done/total chunk-row counts); there is NO independent frontier store to drift. □(FrontierState == derive_frontier_state(rows)). The derived view is A.24's highest-rung join (UNIFY) — it cannot diverge from what it derives.

Frontier immutability post-PLAN — once planned, no unit row is created outside the PLAN claim, so the availability predicates read a STABLE ``total`` and can never PREMATURE-finalize. □(planned ⇒ EXHAUSTED requires total>0 ∧ done>=total): a hypothetical late row only DELAYS EXHAUSTED (raises total), never advances it, and a zero-unit frontier (the R1-impossible total==0) is never EXHAUSTED (design §4.5).

PLAN claim atomicity + claim-once (Ph1b R1) — the PLAN arm claims via a ``planned_at IS NULL`` SQL-CAS and stamps ``planned_at`` ATOMICALLY inside the bulk-create transaction, under Cloud-Tasks at-least-once redelivery + concurrent plan-<job> deliveries. Two safety obligations: (3a) □ ¬(planned_at ∧ total==0) — never a planned-but-no-rows window (``bulk_create_chunk_jobs`` is NOT idempotent: fresh uuids, no (parent,chunk_index) unique key); (3b) □ at-most-one plan worker creates the rows (the CAS admits one; a second create would DUPLICATE the frontier).

FINALIZE triple-fence single-execution — at most one FINALIZE effectively completes per job under concurrent last-finishers + the recovery sweep (Ph1b R2) + Cloud-Tasks redelivery. □ merged_count <= 1, held by three fences: (1) finalize-<job> task name-dedup collapses the enqueues to ≤1 durable task, (2) the merge-claim SQL-CAS admits one deliverer, (3) the positive ``merge_completed_at`` signal idempotency-checks a redelivery. STRICTLY STRONGER than today's dedup-less Pub/Sub completer fan-in (CAS-only, no name-dedup — design §4.6).
DB-is-truth / Redis-is-derived — every authoritative datum (job status / account / billing / analytics) lives in Postgres; Redis holds only ephemeral rebuildable signals.

update_job compare-and-set guard — a conditional status transition (expected_status=X, status=Y) applies iff the row is in X; a losing racer sees rows_updated==0 and never overwrites the winner (the chunk mirror writes ONLY when the CAS won).

Upload-before-DB-update on the corrupt-output fallback — the fallback file is uploaded to remote storage BEFORE status='completed' is written, so a crash between the two never leaves a completed row pointing at a missing artifact.

Migration advisory-lock mutual exclusion — at most ONE process runs schema migrations at a time; the exclusion (pg_advisory_xact_lock / pg_try_advisory_lock on _MIGRATION_LOCK_ID) is held for the whole migration body across the ~4-pod concurrent boot.

Migration-block error isolation — each block commits/rolls-back independently (SAVEPOINT in xact mode, per-block commit in bypass); a failed _migrate_* block is logged+swallowed without aborting the rest, but the seed-invariant assertion is fail-LOUD.

Column-allowlist ↔ CAS interpolation soundness — every column name f-string-interpolated into the update_job/update_chunk SET clause MUST be in the closed _VALID_*_UPDATE_COLUMNS allowlist (an invalid column raises ValueError before any SQL runs).

Schema-drift floor — every column in _VALID_*_UPDATE_COLUMNS corresponds to a column actually present in the Alembic-managed schema (ORM D3b: schema authority is Alembic + the Phase-2 models, not the retired migrations.py DDL chain); a pinned-but-unlanded column is a drift finding, not a silent write-failure.

Connection dispatch soundness — a pgbouncer (transaction-pool) URL ALWAYS routes to xact-lock mode (is_bypass=False) and a direct-postgres URL routes to bypass mode (is_bypass=True); the wrong mode drops the session lock at COMMIT (the pre-260505 bug).

SOA-cost immediate-durability — every SOA-call return folds its (genai_usd, compute_usd) into the per-job Redis accumulator (HINCRBYFLOAT) synchronously at the return site, never buffered in worker memory across the next step (the 'lose at most ONE in-flight step' durability bar).

Both-terminals cost flush — flush_soa_cost_to_job_row is invoked from BOTH the COMPLETING and the FAILED chunk-terminal on_enter hooks; a FAILED job's cost-to-date IS billed (partial-completion). A success-path-only flush silently drops FAILED-job spend.

Flush idempotency — _flush_soa_cost is an atomic Redis HGETALL+DELETE pipeline, so a rare re-entrant terminal (chunk-merge re-drive) finds an empty hash and folds 0.0, never double-counting spend into jobs.cost_usd.

short_description: Exit-code fidelity — handle_cli_result maps every value in the closed CLI exit-code set to exactly one terminal, with no fall-through gap.
full_description: Exit-code fidelity — handle_cli_result maps every value in the closed CLI exit-code set to exactly one terminal, with no fall-through gap. The mapping is DETERMINISTIC (same code+markers ⇒ same terminal) and TOTAL (rule #14 — an unhandled code cannot silently succeed).

C#↔Python exit-code table consistency — the Python CLI_EXIT_* constants EQUAL the C# producer's exit codes (Program.cs + ServiceShouldHaveWorkedException/PerPassValidator .ExitCode). A drift (C# emits an exit code Python doesn't enumerate) silently routes the new code to GENERIC_FAIL — the exit-code analogue of 'a regex subtly wrong for months'. ⚠️ ALREADY DRIFTED: C# exit 4 (ServiceShouldHaveWorkedException) has NO Python constant → G3 shared-map is the by-construction fix (phase-2 design).

short_description: Chunk cost fan-in sums to parent
full_description: Chunk cost fan-in sums to parent — for a chunked parent job, persist_parent_cost_from_chunks sums cost_usd (+ tokens, time) over ALL chunk rows (including FAILED/skipped — partial-completion is billed) into the parent row: jobs.cost_usd == Σ(chunk costs). A dropped chunk is an undercount (the P15 measure-one-level-deeper invariant — the number that drives engineering must equal the invoice).

Atomic chunk-row creation (C5-a) — split_*_into_chunks create ALL chunk rows via one bulk_create_chunk_jobs(specs) transaction: N specs ⇒ N rows in the same order, or 0 rows on any failure (never a partial set). A mid-loop failure rolls the whole batch back (the connection's commit is never called).

Re-drivable chunk publish (C5-b) — dispatch_chunk_jobs publishes ALL chunk specs through a bulk publish whose RETURN CONTRACT is a re-drivable missing-set: the exact specs with NO durable task after the call. The Redis plane satisfies it via one publish_chunks_bulk Lua EVAL (multi-ZADD + per-member ZSCORE-verify, the returned missing-set = the specs that failed the ZSCORE verify); the Cloud Run MANAGED plane satisfies the SAME contract via a re-drivable, idempotent per-chunk create keyed on the durable chunk-ROW set (name-dedup convergent) — the missing-set = the specs left un-enqueued, re-driven to complete BEFORE the parent enters WAITING. ⚠️ RE-ANCHORED (chunk-fanout-liveness-fix Phase 4 M1, REVISE-2): the pre-Epic predicate named a per-chunk publish LOOP impossible and was BLIND to the managed plane (satisfy_ref was Redis-only) — the exact model→as-built drift that let the live 3-chunk-stuck-at-1/3 stranding be declared impossible. The PARITY of the two impls' return contract is held at a parity CONTROL (a shared property test both pass; §G4 — UNIFY unaffordable: Redis Lua EVAL vs Cloud Tasks HTTP creates share the contract, not a body). Near-duplicate of INV-RC-5 (the Redis-comm-plane view of the SAME publish contract) — both intentionally retained + both re-anchored (F-A).

short_description: Chunk purge on every cleanup path (C5-c)
full_description: Chunk purge on every cleanup path (C5-c) — every parent-cleanup path (cancel, stale-sweep) purges the parent's chunks from ALL Redis queue structures via the canonical purge_parent_chunks_from_redis seam; CHECKING/AWAITING_CHECK chunks live in the quota-gate queues and are otherwise leaked. ⚠️ AS-BUILT (Phase-2 AUDIT, §G-4): the content-validation-fail path calls lifecycle.delete_chunks (DB rows + store blobs) but NOT purge_parent_chunks_from_redis — a DIVERGENT (complementary, not equivalent) contract → routed [FIX]+[LINT] (design §6 Q-C).

short_description: strip-attribution precedes finalize, never on failed jobs (C5-d)
full_description: strip-attribution precedes finalize, never on failed jobs (C5-d) — in _finalize_merge_output, _strip_attribution_before_delivery runs BEFORE store.finalize_output, and only on non-failed jobs (a strip that flips status to FAILED short-circuits the finalize). Debug attribution never ships.

Content-fidelity gate: input ⊆ output (C5-e, C5-f) — the merged output passes the 3-gate sequence (integrity → openability → content-validator) IN ORDER before delivery; the content-validator enforces input content ⊆ output content. A fidelity failure drives _handle_content_validation_failure (purge + archive + fail-job — never silent-degrade, MISSION fidelity). CROSS-LANG (§G-3): the gate DECISION is Python (anchored here); the PREDICATE (input ⊆ output) is the C# ContentValidator.Validate — an ACCEPTED_UNMEASURED tail (claimed, not Python-measured) WITH a navigable C#-pointer in the ACCEPTED_UNMEASURED allowlist below.

Per-pass fidelity marker surfaces + gates (C5-g) — the per-pass fidelity signal is a TYPED marker, not a magic string: ##PASS_FIDELITY##:{json} on CLI stderr is parsed via _PASS_FIDELITY_MARKER and routed by CLI_EXIT_PASS_FIDELITY in handle_cli_result; a malformed payload degrades attribution to 'unknown' rather than crashing (fail-loud-but-bounded). STAGING-only gate.

short_description: PDF chunk-boundary tiling is a deterministic total closure (C5-EXTENSION split)
full_description: PDF chunk-boundary tiling is a deterministic total closure (C5-EXTENSION split) — compute_pdf_chunk_boundaries partitions [1..page_count] into contiguous, non-overlapping, gap-free pages_per_chunk-sized ranges whose union is the whole document (every page appears in exactly one chunk). The split stage that feeds work→finalize→merge; a boundary gap/overlap silently drops or double-processes pages. PURE (no I/O) — the tiling closure is the load-bearing invariant.

short_description: Partial-completion COLUMN is source-of-truth; the envelope mirror is faithful (C5-EXTENSION finalize)
full_description: Partial-completion COLUMN is source-of-truth; the envelope mirror is faithful (C5-EXTENSION finalize) — _persist_partial_completion_count writes the partial_completion_count COLUMN (the SoT, architect §7 Q2/Q5 Option B) as images_failed + font_not_avail + font_failed; _compute_partial_count_for_envelope derives the envelope MIRROR from the SAME three buckets, so the customer-facing 3-state 'partial' signal never diverges from the durable column. Fragmentation is a SEPARATE column in both (not folded). VERIFIED CONSISTENT (brief bug-watch): column writer ≡ envelope mirror on partial_completion_count — no lost-state drift.

short_description: Chunk-eligibility decision is pure + hot-config-safe; downsample dispatch is decision-gated (C5-EXTENSION decision)
full_description: Chunk-eligibility decision is pure + hot-config-safe; downsample dispatch is decision-gated (C5-EXTENSION decision) — classify_chunk_eligibility is a PURE function of (input_size_mb, page_count, size_threshold, page_threshold) → ChunkTrigger, with NO I/O or config read; the threshold accessors get_{size,page}_chunk_threshold* read runtime_config.current() at CALL time so a POST /api/admin/config flip takes effect on the NEXT job without drifting an in-flight decision. _maybe_run_downsample is the coordinator entry gated on that decision. VERIFIED (brief bug-watch): no threshold-drift — the live-config read is per-call.

short_description: Dynamic chunk-threshold probe is bounded + fail-safe (F1-fix contract)
full_description: Dynamic chunk-threshold probe is bounded + fail-safe (F1-fix contract) — get_dynamic_chunk_threshold reads the live GenAI-service /v1/capacity utilization at CALL time (via the typed ServiceClient seam) and returns a threshold CLAMPED to [CHUNK_THRESHOLD_MIN, CHUNK_THRESHOLD_MAX]: idle -> chunk aggressively, busy -> larger chunks. EVERY failure edge (no GENAI_SERVICE_URL, non-ok response, ValidationError, any Exception) returns the caller's `default` — the probe is best-effort (chunk tuning is non-essential; the default is always safe), so a capacity-probe failure NEVER crashes the job. DISTINCT from INV-C5X-3's decision.py classify_chunk_eligibility (the PURE force-chunk classifier that CONSUMES a threshold value); this is the live-capacity probe that PRODUCES the tuned value.

short_description: CLI-subprocess argv-BUILD goes through the typed AdaToolInvoker chokepoint (rule #52 typed-invoker)
full_description: CLI-subprocess argv-BUILD goes through the typed AdaToolInvoker chokepoint (rule #52 typed-invoker) — _build_cli_command assembles the remediate/check/analyze argv via AdaToolInvoker.resolved().remediate(...), NEVER a hand-built list, so a per-format flag set cannot silently drift; the format->command mapping is TOTAL (lookup_format raises ValueError on an unsupported ext — rule #14 no silent fall-through). This is the argv-BUILD complement to C2's INV-C2-4 (handle_cli_result — the exit-code DECODE side): C2 anchored the RESULT/marker end of the CLI-subprocess seam, this anchors the COMMAND end. The re-exported private argv helpers (_append_sm_prefs_flags / _maybe_append_audience_level / _maybe_write_user_context_tempfile) live canonically in command.py (P8 anti-shim: pipeline.py no longer carries them — A.7).

CLI-subprocess drive-side observability + trace provenance — forward_cli_summary_lines relays the child CLI's ##SUMMARY## lines to the worker log (the diagnosability leg — rule #53), and persist_trace_artifact durably persists the per-job GenAI trace directory as a job artifact (the provenance leg). The process-DRIVE complement to C2's RESULT-decode (handle_cli_result) and INV-C6-3's argv-BUILD (command.py): the three together model the full CLI-subprocess seam (BUILD argv -> DRIVE/stream -> DECODE result). cluster-5 [AUDIT] handoff (phase-3-remeasure §4 assigned the test to cluster-5; the runner residue is the CLI-subprocess family, cluster-6).

Fleet-concurrency display sourcing — the admin-dashboard fleet-concurrency figure is sourced from the per-vendor Redis AIMD `active` gauge (the authoritative cross-worker in-flight GenAI-request count), NEVER from the per-job `genai_worker_fanout_cap` column or its MAX aggregate. That per-job column is a CONFIG ECHO (the worker's fixed C4 fan-out cap), structurally blind to cross-worker fleet overlap; re-aggregating it and presenting it as an observed fleet metric is exactly the bug this Epic corrected. The Phase-2 relabel confined the aggregate to the honest `max_worker_fanout_cap_configured` key (config echo, never a fleet peak); INV-OBS-1 posture A pins that it STAYS honest — the proof-of-fire NEGATIVE test goes RED if a future edit re-sources the fleet figure from the per-job column (e.g. re-aliasing the MAX aggregate back to a `*concurrency_current` fleet-observation name).

short_description: Fleet-signal / state-view DECOUPLING + reconciliation bound (Q2 LINEAR modelling)
full_description: Fleet-signal / state-view DECOUPLING + reconciliation bound (Q2 LINEAR modelling) — the AIMD `active` fleet signal (unit: in-flight GenAI *requests*) and the JobStateMachine in-flight view (unit: *chunks*) are DECOUPLED: no pipeline transition cross-reads AIMD / capacity (phase-1b §D confirmed pipeline.py reads neither in any transition), so the two counters cannot double-count. The reconciliation bound `active_v <= (in-flight chunks) * C4 <= C3 * C4` and `active_v <= ceiling_v` holds, decoupling the request-unit fleet signal from the chunk-unit state view. Modelled as a LINEAR decoupling ASSERTION (single worker lane, coord=NONE), NOT the N-worker concurrent-acquire envelope race: the envelope-safety leg (`active_v` never exceeds `ceiling_v` under N parallel try_acquire) is the AIMD limiter's OWN safety property, owned + exercised by services/genai-service/test_aimd_property.py + test_aimd_storm_debounce.py — CITED, NOT re-homed here (re-homing would derive SAFETY_BFS and spuriously mandate a redundant simworld; Q2 ruling).

short_description: Credit debit-once CAS + consume⇒ledger fidelity (money conservation)
full_description: Credit debit-once CAS + consume⇒ledger fidelity (money conservation) — the consume_group_credits atomic decrement (UPDATE groups SET credit_balance = credit_balance - %s WHERE id = %s AND credit_balance >= %s RETURNING) admits AT MOST ONE debit per coverable balance across N concurrent consumers (a losing racer sees row is None → False, no double-spend), AND every committed decrement pairs with exactly one matching-sign credit_ledger_v2 row in the SAME txn (a committed decrement with no ledger row — the torn CAS-then-ledger sink — is unreachable). The money-path analogue of C1's INV-P2 (CAS + dependent mirror), and a DISTINCT CAS site from INV-14's upstream jobs-row quota credit-fence (INV-14 prevents double-INVOKING the consume; INV-PS-1 prevents concurrent consumes double-SPENDING the balance) — genuinely warranted, not redundant.

Sidecar upsert idempotency (converge) — the idempotent-write sidecar seams re-apply a logical write as a no-op-equivalent (converge to the same row state, never a duplicate row or a lost update): cold_start/document_telemetry/config_overrides via a single-statement ON CONFLICT (<key>) DO UPDATE, and upsert_user_oauth via a read-then-branch (SELECT → UPDATE-existing / INSERT-new) that is idempotent on the email key. A retry / re-delivery of the same write converges — C1's idempotency contract applied to the sidecar upserts.

Analytics is DB-authoritative append (the store-split) — every analytics/activity/telemetry write (record_analytics / record_daily_job / log_activity) targets Postgres as the authoritative store; none treats a Redis value as truth. A failed analytics write is best-effort (fire-and-forget) and never blocks the request path — C1's INV-P1 store-split applied to the analytics sidecar. DISTINCT from INV-P1 (which anchors only jobs.py::update_job) — anchors the analytics WRITERS (G-Q4 KEEP distinct, ratified).

short_description: Persistence layer issues NO Redis cleanup (the layering invariant)
full_description: Persistence layer issues NO Redis cleanup (the layering invariant) — the lifecycle.py sweep/expire seams (sweep_stale_active_jobs / expire_stale_queued_jobs / expire_stale_checking_jobs) update DB rows ONLY and return ids for the CALLER (background.py) to Redis-clean; they never call remove_from_all_queues / purge_parent_chunks_from_redis. Inverting this would break the DB-persistence-layer-is-Redis-unaware layering the 4 explicit noqa: cancel-uses-remove-all-queues cites protect — an A.24 invariant-living-only-in-prose (the noqa comment) encoded as a structural test.

short_description: SQL-interpolation floor: every dynamic SQL fragment is enum/allowlist-bounded
full_description: SQL-interpolation floor: every dynamic SQL fragment is enum/allowlist-bounded — analytics_reporting._apply_source appends the analytics source filter ONLY as a parametrized .where(Analytics.source == source.value) bound by the AnalyticsSource enum (portable-db Phase 7 STRENGTHENED the former sql_with_source {src}-marker string-interpolation into a Core parametrized bind — injection now structurally impossible AND no interpolation at all), and document_telemetry.record_document_telemetry builds its dynamic column list ONLY from _DOCUMENT_TELEMETRY_COUNTER_COLUMNS (unknown columns skipped, never interpolated). No user string ever reaches the interpolation — C1's INV-P6 column-allowlist floor generalized to the sidecar SQL-composition seams. POSITIVE finding: the enum-bound is the best-in-class model (arch-4); the runtime-allowlist is sound but weaker — future SQL-composition seams should adopt the enum bound.

short_description: Read-model reads Postgres for authoritative counts
full_description: Read-model reads Postgres for authoritative counts — queue_status.py's read projection (count_by_status / queue_depth / get_active_processing_job_ids) computes its counts from the authoritative Postgres jobs/chunks rows, never from a Redis queue-depth counter (Redis counters are the ephemeral rebuildable scaling SIGNAL, not the correctness truth — C1 INV-P1). The READ side of the store-split; DISTINCT from INV-P1 (G-Q4 KEEP distinct, ratified).

short_description: Sidecar rows carry typed ids (typed-id integrity)
full_description: Sidecar rows carry typed ids (typed-id integrity) — every sidecar durable-row identity is a typed NewType (JobId / UserId / SessionId / GroupId), never a bare str at the seam boundary, so a wrong-id-kind write is a pyright-strict type error, not a silent cross-table row corruption. C1's typed-id contract applied to the sidecar write signatures (create_session(user_id: UserId) -> SessionId; record_debug_failure(job_id: JobId, ...)).

short_description: ContentValidator verdict is fail-CLOSED (hard-gate decision purity)
full_description: ContentValidator verdict is fail-CLOSED (hard-gate decision purity) — _interpret_cli_validate_result maps EVERY input to ok=False UNLESS returncode==0 OR (returncode==1 AND stdout parses as a JSON list of wire-valid ContentValidationViolation): unparseable JSON → ok=False (PARSE_ERROR), non-array → ok=False (NON_ARRAY), exit >= 2 → ok=False (UNEXPECTED_EXIT); a wire-schema-invalid element is REPLACED by a validator-error, never silently dropped. There is NO input for which a content-loss / validator-malfunction produces ok=True — the 'wrong remediation is worse than a slow one' mission axis made mechanical. (Phase-1b §1: CORRECT — pure fn, single lane, no coord primitive; validate.py:800 DEFAULTS ok=False.)

short_description: The content-fidelity gate REACHES the canonical seam on every completing path (reach-completeness
full_description: The content-fidelity gate REACHES the canonical seam on every completing path (reach-completeness — the C5 incomplete-composition invariant applied to this cluster). Every path that transitions a parent job to COMPLETED with a merged output either (a) invokes run_content_validator(input, output) and acts on its verdict, OR (b) is on a DECLARED exception (the input-path-unavailable branch, chunking/merge.py:2231, a warn-and-skip). No completing path reaches only the integrity check (validate_output_integrity) while silently skipping the fidelity gate. EXPLOITABILITY (Phase-1b §2, RESOLVED): not-exploitable on a healthy job — no pre-merge input-deletion path exists (GcsJobStore persists jobs/{parent}/input.* durably; cleanup_job never deletes the GCS input blob; the completer is idempotent on an already-completed parent via PURGED_AFTER_COMPLETE), so falsy-at-merge ⟺ an already-anomalous storage state where fail is the only alternative anyway — a declared exception, LOW severity. Optional fail-closed hardening [FIX] floated (defense-in-depth), NOT mandatory.

short_description: Output-integrity classification is fail-closed per format (corruption-gate purity)
full_description: Output-integrity classification is fail-closed per format (corruption-gate purity) — _classify_integrity(ext, facts) returns ok=False for a ZIP with a CRC error OR a missing required root entry ([Content_Types].xml etc.), and for a PDF whose header is not %PDF OR whose CLI parse failed; it returns ok=True ONLY on a clean structural check (or an UNKNOWN_FORMAT skip). A corrupt output NEVER classifies OK for a known format. (Phase-1b §1: CORRECT — a small closed pure fn over (ext, facts).)

short_description: Advisory validation NEVER fails a job (the advisory-vs-hard-gate boundary) — no code path inside web/a11yvalidate/* transitions a job to FAILED.
full_description: Advisory validation NEVER fails a job (the advisory-vs-hard-gate boundary) — no code path inside web/a11yvalidate/* transitions a job to FAILED. The accessibility judge and the SSIM rendered-fidelity check are advisory-only (they write jobs.report.* rollups, never status=FAILED); _run_rendered_fidelity_check returns None on every disabled/unreachable/error branch and NEVER raises past the caller; _run_a11y_validation returns a typed outcome, never a job-failure. This is the single most product-load-bearing semantic of the cluster (a wrong flattening lies about failure behavior — §1a). The model DECLARES the failure-semantics boundary (G-Q1 RATIFIED first-class INV); the existing lint-a11yvalidate-canonical.py (bans db.update_job(status=FAILED) in the subpackage) POLICES re-introduction — architecture + control, A.21/A.22 defense-in-depth.

short_description: Editor round-trip is a durable EditorRoundTripState lifecycle (IR_FETCHED → EDIT_APPLIED → RECHECKED → SAVED) with a canonical_hash SAVE-FENCE
full_description: Editor round-trip is a durable EditorRoundTripState lifecycle (IR_FETCHED → EDIT_APPLIED → RECHECKED → SAVED) with a canonical_hash SAVE-FENCE — the STATE-MACHINE model the Phase-1b review forced (§3 G-Q3, reviewer WINS). The round-trip carries DURABLE cross-request state: an editor-oplog.jsonl oplog (accumulates edit intent across requests), a persisted output.editor-edited.pdf GCS variant, and canonical_hash (the save-idempotence seed). The SAVE transition (_run_editor_save's trial-apply→append_oplog→CheckpointDeriver.publish) carries a version fence: the base it edited still matches the persisted checkpoint generation (if_generation_match CAS), fail-loud / recompute-on-412 otherwise. ✅ AS-BUILT (A.18): the fence is NOW PRESENT — Option-B B-2 (editor-download-edit-loss-repro-260904) made the checkpoint a pure DERIVED CACHE of the oplog: every save full-replays dedup(oplog) onto the pristine output and publishes under a generation-guarded CAS-or-recompute loop, so two concurrent editor edits CONVERGE (no lost-update, no last-write-wins clobber) — closing the prior UNFENCED reads-original-base race this invariant pinned. The round-trip ALSO fails LOUD on transport errors (apply_editor_edit raises DocEditServiceError on non-2xx/missing-body, never silently returns unedited bytes) and the recheck leg re-validates the EDITED bytes, never the pre-edit bytes.

short_description: The A11yBatchAccumulator converges under concurrent judge callers (the HAIRY row → SAFETY_BFS).
full_description: The A11yBatchAccumulator converges under concurrent judge callers (the HAIRY row → SAFETY_BFS). The accumulator — a threading.Lock-guarded shared _buckets/_timers structure that N concurrent judge callers append into, each blocking on a per-entry threading.Event, flushed by EITHER a size-trigger (len(bucket) >= batch_size) OR a threading.Timer — admits NO lost entry and NO double-flush: every enqueued entry is flushed exactly once and its waiting caller is signaled exactly once, whether the flush fires by size or by timer, and the size-trigger racing the timer never double-processes a bucket nor strands a caller's Event unset. (Phase-1b §1: CORRECT at SAFETY_BFS — genuine in-process concurrency, batch.py:114-161.)

short_description: Metric-consistency: every total-depth queue metric reads ALL active queue structures FOR ITS SCOPE (the arch-rule, encoded)
full_description: Metric-consistency: every total-depth queue metric reads ALL active queue structures FOR ITS SCOPE (the arch-rule, encoded) — any function whose result is a 'total queue depth' / 'aggregate demand' signal reads EVERY structure in the active-queue set for its DECISION-scope: the MAIN_QUEUE read (RedisQueue.queue_depth, the metrics:queue_depth rebuild source) reads 4 buckets + chunks (quota-gate deliberately excluded to match the counter's incr scope). A reader that reads a strict SUBSET of its scope's active structures is the silent-under-report the CLAUDE.md arch-rule forbids (the historical LIST→sorted-sets migration that left the scaler reading only the chunks ZSET). ⚠️ AS-BUILT: the metrics:queue_depth STRING counter drifts high (chunk publishes incr it at queue.py:442/499 but chunk pops never decr it; the sole decr, job_introducer.py, fires on parent-claim only) — bounded by sync_from_db rebuilds; the divergence is ALREADY known/worked-around at admin_dashboard.py (a WHY-comment routes the KPI around the counter), leaving only /api/admin/stats served-raw. That is a separately-tagged product [FIX] (Phase-1b §7), NOT this row (this row encodes the SUBSET-read completeness contract, a DISTINCT class from the incr/decr asymmetry).

short_description: Schema is the sole raw-Redis key registry (the boundary invariant)
full_description: Schema is the sole raw-Redis key registry (the boundary invariant) — every Redis key any component writes/reads is DECLARED in web/dispatch/schema.py (a schema class or key-builder), and only the dispatch/ package constructs raw Redis clients / issues raw ZSET/Lua ops. A key literal assembled outside the schema (bypassing the RedisKey factory) is a violation. This row ANCHORS the EXISTING lint-web-dispatch-boundary.py into the queryable model so 'how is the raw-Redis boundary enforced?' is answerable from the model (a how-is-this-enforced answer + drift guard), not new verification.

'Redis for communication, DB for truth' — live/ephemeral signals (queue depth, dispatch queues, progress percent, heartbeats, running metrics) live in Redis; durable state (jobs, accounts, billing) lives in Postgres. No component treats a Redis value as the authoritative durable truth; Redis loss DEGRADES signals, never CORRUPTS durable state. Terminal progress is archived to jobs.percent_done at COMPLETED (the TTL'd progress HASH is self-cleaning if a job terminates without explicit cleanup). The REDIS side of the store-split C1's INV-P1 anchors on the DB side.

short_description: Cancellation removes a job from ALL queue structures (the completeness invariant)
full_description: Cancellation removes a job from ALL queue structures (the completeness invariant) — remove_from_all_queues(job_id) removes the job from EVERY structure it could be in (4 size buckets + chunks + processing + 2 quota-gate LISTs + the in-flight lease) so a cancelled job is never popped by a worker and never pins a warm worker via a lingering lease. Missing ANY structure leaves a dangling entry (the CHECKING/AWAITING_CHECK class the quota-gate LISTs cover — CLAUDE.md's cancellation-requires-Redis-cleanup rule). The QueueDepthScope.CANCEL_COMPLETENESS scope — walks the SAME active-queue structure set INV-RC-1 enumerates (Phase-1b §5 DRY: one canonical enumeration, two invariants read it).

short_description: Chunk creation is bulk-atomic; chunk publish is re-drivable to completeness
full_description: Chunk creation is bulk-atomic; chunk publish is re-drivable to completeness — production chunk-row creation goes through db.bulk_create_chunk_jobs(list[ChunkJobSpec]) (one atomic transaction, INV-19) and publish through publish_chunks_bulk. On the Redis plane the publish is a single Lua EVAL (ZADD-N-then-verify, atomic WITHIN one publish); on the Cloud Run MANAGED plane the publish is an idempotent per-chunk create whose COMPLETENESS is restored by a re-drive keyed on the durable chunk-ROW set (name-dedup convergent). The load-bearing property is COMPLETENESS-eventually (no chunk spec is permanently un-enqueued), NOT 'never a per-chunk loop'. ⚠️ RE-ANCHORED (chunk-fanout-liveness-fix Phase 4 M1, REVISE-2 / F-A): the pre-Epic predicate literally named the managed per-chunk-loop partial-fanout hazard IMPOSSIBLE ('no per-chunk publish loop in a production path … a crash mid-loop leaves N published and M unpublished with no atomic boundary') and was BLIND to the managed plane (Redis-only satisfy_refs) — the SECOND invariant carrying the identical blindness as INV-20 (the Redis-comm-plane VIEW of the SAME publish contract). Both are intentionally retained (distinct model VIEWS) + both re-anchored to cover the managed plane. Reconciles with the CLAUDE.md 'Chunk creation + publish are bulk-atomic' architecture bullet.

short_description: Progress writes are Lua-atomic monotonic (percent never regresses under concurrent chunk-worker aggregation)
full_description: Progress writes are Lua-atomic monotonic (percent never regresses under concurrent chunk-worker aggregation) — every progress-HASH write (set_parent_progress / set_chunk_progress) is a Lua-atomic compare-and-set that only ADVANCES pct (a later tick reporting a LOWER pct is a no-op) and normalizes stage_detail through the closed ProgressStage set (_normalize_stage). N chunk workers write into their parent's aggregate: aggregate_parent_from_chunks reads sibling chunk HASHes via a NON-transactional pipeline, computes the weighted average in Python, THEN calls the CAS — the read-compute-write spans three steps across ≥2 lanes, so the race is NOT contained in one EVAL. A raw HGETALL-then-HSET without the CAS would let a stale tick regress the bar; the SimWorld must prove the COMPOSITION (monotonic-CAS + phase-floor UP-clamp + stale-sibling aggregate) holds under ALL interleavings (Phase-1b §3).

short_description: 'processing' is DERIVED from llen(PROCESSING_KEY), never a rival counter
full_description: 'processing' is DERIVED from llen(PROCESSING_KEY), never a rival counter — the in-flight count is ALWAYS llen(ProcessingQueue.KEY) (the reservation LIST), never a maintained STRING counter. A LIST length is structurally >= 0 (the LREM-idempotent contract); a mirror counter drifts NEGATIVE under uncoordinated decrements (the historical -7/-9 staging bug). Re-introducing a metrics:processing counter is the violation. This row ANCHORS the EXISTING lint-no-raw-processing-counter.py into the model — the deliberate ABSENCE of a Metrics.PROCESSING member made a queryable, drift-guarded invariant.

short_description: Redis keys carry typed ids (typed-id integrity)
full_description: Redis keys carry typed ids (typed-id integrity) — every schema key-builder returns RedisKey (assembled with config.REDIS_PREFIX); every job/chunk-scoped key-builder takes a JobId / ChunkId; metrics functions accept the typed vocabulary (WorkerPid, CounterName, A11yOutcome, ProgressStage). A key assembled from a raw str that skipped the RedisKey factory (wrong/absent prefix → cross-env key collision) is the violation. This row ANCHORS the pyright-strict gate + the existing typed-id DDT into the model.

Parent-rollup cost conservation — a chunked parent's jobs.cost_usd EQUALS the SUM of its chunk rows' cost_usd (persist_parent_cost_from_chunks, called once at _coordinate_merge finalize). Rollup is a single sequential fold over the chunk rows; every chunk that ran the CLI (even a FAILED/partial chunk) contributes its accumulated cost (partial-completion IS billed). No chunk is double-counted (each chunk row read once) and none is dropped (a NULL cost row contributes 0, still counted as a contributor for tokens).

short_description: Per-model spend conservation (SPEND-6) — for any job, SUM(job_model_costs.cost_usd) EQUALS jobs.cost_usd.
full_description: Per-model spend conservation (SPEND-6) — for any job, SUM(job_model_costs.cost_usd) EQUALS jobs.cost_usd. persist_job_cost_usd writes the aggregate jobs.cost_usd AND the per-model breakdown rows from the SAME ##TOKEN_USAGE## marker (both priced by the single genai-pricing.json spine, computed C#-side), so the breakdown can never diverge from the aggregate. An empty per_model list is a GenAI-free / legacy-CLI no-op (0 == 0 holds).

SpendReader never-false-zero (SPEND-3) — a spend read over an empty range returns an EMPTY list (rendered as SpendSource.NONE / 'no data'), NEVER a fabricated $0.00 row. SpendReader is the SOLE durable read seam (SPEND-1): it SUMs already-priced usd from Postgres and never computes a rate. A DB error degrades to [] (logged by the persistence _with_retry — not a silent catch, A.14), so the admin panel labels 'no data' rather than lying.

short_description: Debit-once (NEW-GAP-4) — convert_reservation_to_debit debits a job's reservation AT MOST ONCE across concurrent + redelivered deliveries.
full_description: Debit-once (NEW-GAP-4) — convert_reservation_to_debit debits a job's reservation AT MOST ONCE across concurrent + redelivered deliveries. The fence is the clear_job_reservation SQL CAS (UPDATE jobs SET reserved_credits=0 ... WHERE id=%s AND reserved_credits>0 RETURNING ...): the FIRST convert clears the row and debits the group balance + writes ONE ledger row; every redelivered/concurrent convert finds reserved_credits already 0 (0 rows RETURNED) → debits NOTHING. Debit-once by job-id — the double-charge class an AT-LEAST-ONCE queue bridge introduces.

Cancel-once terminal-consistency (NEW-GAP-3) — JobLifecycle.cancel CASes the terminal write on the status the caller READ (UPDATE jobs SET status='cancelled' ... WHERE id=%s AND status=%s). A concurrent/redelivered cancel that loses the race sees rows==0 → idempotent no-op (runs NO side effects). Exactly ONE caller fires the reservation-release + Redis/chunk purge; a CANCELLED row never carries a FAILED side-effect bundle (cancel-vs-fail consistency).

Credit-grant equalization — the anonymous per-cookie grant (ANON_GRANT_CREDITS) EQUALS the signed-up free-tier seed (SIGNUP_FREE_CREDITS), both $5-worth at CREDIT_PRICE_CENTS (no-commercialization-mode Q2). ANON_GRANT_CREDITS is COMPUTED (5*100 // CREDIT_PRICE_CENTS), not env-overridable, so it stays consistent with the customer-facing pricing surface; a price change moves both grants together. credit_constants is a DB-free leaf so the equalization is pure-math pin-testable.

Binding env/brief-completeness — every canonical dispatch supplies the dispatch-id to the sentinel (via ADA_TOOL_DISPATCH_ID env OR the brief-file dispatch-id: line), so update_harness_id fires. The §2.3 env-only drop is a violation.

Binding liveness — every registered dispatch is eventually bound: its register event is followed by an update-harness-id for the same dispatch-id within the pre-sentinel window. Modeled single-lane (each agent's own ordered register→sentinel handoff) → LINEAR (§G-Q6).

Binding uniqueness/no-mis-join — at most one harness_id is bound to a given dispatch_id, and it is the OWNING agent's, never a sibling's, under concurrent dispatch. The rejected Option-1 content-join would introduce the mis-join race.

short_description: Marker↔registry consistency — once bound, the active-agents marker key and the registry row's canonical key resolve to the SAME agent (J2/J5 no longer mis-key).
full_description: Marker↔registry consistency — once bound, the active-agents marker key and the registry row's canonical key resolve to the SAME agent (J2/J5 no longer mis-key). A single ordered reconcile once bound → LINEAR (§G-Q6 c).

short_description: S8 fan-in measurement causality — for every job jobs.completer_claimed_at >= jobs.chunk_notified_at (S8 >= 0).
full_description: S8 fan-in measurement causality — for every job jobs.completer_claimed_at >= jobs.chunk_notified_at (S8 >= 0). The two stamps are UNGUARDED cross-pod writes (the completer merge-claim is gated on the chunk COUNT, not on the chunk_notified_at stamp), so a NEGATIVE S8 is reachable and MUST be flagged by the reader's measurement-integrity gate, never averaged into a reported latency.

short_description: S8 fan-in start stamp reflects the LAST chunk — jobs.chunk_notified_at holds the fan-in-complete instant, not a racing earlier chunk.
full_description: S8 fan-in start stamp reflects the LAST chunk — jobs.chunk_notified_at holds the fan-in-complete instant, not a racing earlier chunk. Race-free BY CONSTRUCTION: concurrent per-chunk stamps serialise on the parent ROW LOCK and SERVER_NOW binds now() (txn-start = the stamp UPDATE = the txn's first statement), so the last committer writes MAX(now()) = the last chunk. Depends on the stamp remaining a single-statement update_job with no preceding same-txn read (else now() pins early).

S8 fan-in measurement completeness — every job that reaches COMPLETED EVENTUALLY has BOTH jobs.chunk_notified_at and jobs.completer_claimed_at stamped; a terminal job missing either is a measurement GAP the reader flags (an unstamped completed job = a dark S8, never a silent zero).
